binders: There exists a real constant C.
Within the final conjunct, σ ranges universally over all real numbers.
hypotheses: The σ-dependent conclusion is required under the hypothesis σ≥0.
conclusions: The infimum-defined exponential-square scale of id under gaussianReal(0,1) is at most ENNReal.ofReal(C), hence at most C because C>0.
For every real σ≥0, the same scale of id under gaussianReal(0,σ^2) is at most ENNReal.ofReal(Cσ), hence at most Cσ.
mathematical_definitions: For a measure μ on Ω and X:Ω→Real, define Q(μ,X)=inf {t∈ENNReal | X is measurable, t≠0, t≠∞, exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) dμ≤2}.
ENNReal is [0,∞] and ENNReal.ofReal(r) embeds max(r,0).
gaussianReal(μ,v) is Dirac mass at μ when the nonnegative parameter v is 0, and otherwise is Lebesgue measure with density gaussianPDF(μ,v).
The random variable id is the coordinate function x↦x on the Borel real line.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is one positive real constant C such that Q(gaussianReal(0,1),id)≤C and, simultaneously, for every nonnegative real σ, Q(gaussianReal(0,σ^2),id)≤Cσ, where Q is the infimum of finite nonzero scales t for which the identity is measurable and exp(id^2/t^2) is integrable with integral at most 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The σ-dependent assertion is restricted to σ≥0; negative σ are excluded by the implication and impose no obligation.
The same witness C must work for every σ≥0; C cannot depend on σ.
The Gaussian parameter is the NNReal value σ^2, while the upper bound is linear in σ.
At σ=0 the measure is Dirac mass at 0 and the right-hand side is 0, so the statement forces Q for this degenerate case to be 0.
Admissible scales explicitly exclude 0 and ∞, but their infimum can still be 0 and need not itself be admissible or attained.
LocalDef001 is only the raw ENNReal infimum; it does not separately assert that the admissible set is nonempty. If the set were empty, complete-lattice infimum semantics would govern the value.
The bound is on the infimum Q, not directly a claim that t=C or t=Cσ satisfies the exponential-moment condition.
The first bound is mathematically repeated by the universal bound at σ=1, assuming the displayed Gaussian parameters are identified definitionally.
No numerical value, optimality, or lower bound for C is asserted.
Although ENNReal.ofReal truncates negative inputs to 0, the explicit assumptions C>0 and σ≥0 prevent truncation from weakening the displayed bounds.
ambiguities: The body of gaussianPDF is outside the supplied semantic frontier, so the packet does not by itself determine whether gaussianReal's nonnegative parameter v is conventionally called variance, standard deviation, or another Gaussian scale; the exact formal translation therefore retains gaussianReal(0,v), with v=1 or v=σ^2.

The packet does not expose the special-case definition of the ENNReal infimum of an empty admissible set beyond the supplied complete-order instance chain, though this does not change the literal infimum-based formulation.
